topics.title: Text Properties
topics.summary: Align, decorate, transform and space text; shadows, white-space and drop caps.
topics.description:
CSS has many properties dedicated to how text looks and flows.

### Alignment and decoration
- `text-align`: `left`, `right`, `center`, `justify`.
- `text-decoration`: shorthand for `-line` (underline, overline, line-through), `-color`, `-style` (solid, double, dotted, wavy) and `-thickness`. `text-decoration: none` removes link underlines.
- `text-underline-offset` moves the underline away from the text.
- `text-transform`: `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize`.
- `text-indent` indents the first line.

### Spacing
| Property | Controls |
|---|---|
| `letter-spacing` | space between characters |
| `word-spacing` | space between words |
| `line-height` | distance between lines - use a unitless number like `1.6` |

### white-space and wrapping
- `white-space: nowrap` keeps text on one line.
- `white-space: pre-wrap` preserves line breaks and spaces.
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` / `word-break: break-word` break long words.
- `text-wrap: balance` (modern) evens out heading lines.

### text-shadow
`text-shadow: x y blur color;` e.g. `text-shadow: 2px 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);`. Multiple shadows are comma separated (useful for glow).

### Gradient text
```css
.gradient { background: linear-gradient(90deg,#f06,#48f); -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text; color: transparent; }
```

### Readability tips
- Line length around 45-75 characters (`max-width: 65ch`).
- `line-height` 1.5 to 1.7 for body text.
- Do not justify text on narrow columns (it creates rivers of white space).
keyPoints: text-align, text-decoration, text-transform are the everyday trio
Use unitless line-height (1.5) so it scales with font-size
letter-spacing and word-spacing tune the density
text-shadow takes x y blur color and can be stacked
overflow-wrap/white-space control wrapping
pitfalls: Setting line-height in px on a parent - children inherit the fixed pixel value
Using text-decoration: none on links without another focus/hover clue

interview.q: How do you control spacing between lines of text?
interview.a: With line-height. A unitless value like 1.5 is a multiplier of the element's font-size and is inherited correctly.

interview.q: How do you create a drop cap?
interview.a: Use the ::first-letter pseudo-element, make it larger and often float it left.

interview.q: What is the difference between letter-spacing and word-spacing?
interview.a: letter-spacing changes the gap between characters, word-spacing changes the gap between words.

topics.title: Fonts and Font Properties
topics.summary: font-family stacks, size, weight, style, shorthand and web-safe fallbacks.
topics.description:
### Main font properties
| Property | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `font-family` | `"Urbanist", Arial, sans-serif` | list of fonts, last should be a generic family |
| `font-size` | `1.125rem` | prefer rem |
| `font-weight` | `400`, `700`, `bold` | numeric 100-900 |
| `font-style` | `normal` / `italic` / `oblique` | |
| `font-variant` | `small-caps` | |
| `line-height` | `1.5` | |

### Font stack and fallbacks
If the first font is missing, the browser tries the next. Always end with a **generic family**: `serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `system-ui`.

```css
body {
  font-family: "Urbanist", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
}
```

Quote font names that contain spaces.

### Shorthand
`font: italic small-caps 700 1.25rem/1.5 "Poppins", sans-serif;` - order: style, variant, weight, size/line-height, family. Size and family are **required**.

### Loading fonts
- **Google Fonts**: `<link>` in head (or `@import` - slower).
- **Self hosted**: `@font-face` (see the Fonts and Variable Fonts topic).
- Use `font-display: swap;` to avoid invisible text while the font loads.

### Good practice
- 1-2 font families per site.
- Use a system font stack for speed.
- Set `font-family` once on `body` and let it inherit. Form controls do not inherit by default, so add `button, input { font: inherit; }`.
keyPoints: font-family is a stack that ends with a generic family
font-weight uses 100-900 or keywords normal/bold
font shorthand needs at least size and family
Use rem for size and unitless line-height
Set font on body; make controls inherit with font: inherit
pitfalls: Not providing fallback fonts - layout shifts or ugly default font
Expecting buttons and inputs to inherit the body font automatically

interview.q: What is a fallback font and why is it important?
interview.a: It is the next font in the font-family list used when the preferred one fails to load. It keeps text readable and prevents layout breakage.

interview.q: How do you add a custom font?
interview.a: Define it with @font-face (src url + format) or link a hosted font service, then use its name in font-family.
It shows fallback text immediately and swaps in the custom font when it is ready, avoiding invisible text.

topics.title: Backgrounds
topics.summary: background-color, image, repeat, position, size, attachment, clip and multiple backgrounds.
topics.description:
The background layer paints behind the content, padding and border.

### Longhand properties
| Property | Common values |
|---|---|
| `background-color` | any color |
| `background-image` | `url(...)`, gradients; comma-separated for multiple layers |
| `background-repeat` | `repeat`, `no-repeat`, `repeat-x`, `repeat-y`, `space`, `round` |
| `background-position` | `center`, `top left`, `50% 20%`, `right 10px bottom 10px` |
| `background-size` | `auto`, `cover`, `contain`, `100% 100%` |
| `background-attachment` | `scroll`, `fixed`, `local` |
| `background-clip` | `border-box`, `padding-box`, `content-box`, `text` |
| `background-origin` | where the position box starts |

### cover vs contain
- `cover`: scale so the image fills the box completely (may crop).
- `contain`: scale so the whole image is visible (may leave gaps).

### Multiple backgrounds
Layers are comma separated and the **first one is on top**:

```css
background:
  linear-gradient(rgba(0,0,0,.5), rgba(0,0,0,.5)),  /* overlay on top */
  url("photo.jpg") center / cover no-repeat;
```

### Shorthand
`background: color image repeat position / size attachment;` - note the slash between position and size.

### Parallax-like effect
`background-attachment: fixed;` keeps the image still while the page scrolls (used in the project in this course). It is not supported well on mobile.

### Blend modes
`background-blend-mode: multiply;` mixes layers with each other and with the background color.
keyPoints: background-size: cover fills the box; contain fits the whole image
Multiple backgrounds are comma separated; first is on top
Shorthand writes position / size with a slash
background-attachment: fixed creates a simple parallax
background-clip: text enables gradient text
pitfalls: Using only background-image without a fallback background-color for contrast
Forgetting that the element needs a height to show a background
Overwriting earlier background-* properties with the shorthand later in the rule

topics.title: Gradients
topics.summary: linear, radial, conic and repeating gradients, color stops and overlays.
topics.description:
A **gradient** is an image generated by CSS, used with `background-image` (or `background`). No image file is needed and it scales perfectly.

### linear-gradient
```css
background: linear-gradient(to right, red, yellow);
background: linear-gradient(135deg, #004d7a, #00bf72, #a8eb12);
background: linear-gradient(to bottom right, #004d7a 0%, #a8eb12 100%);
```
Direction can be a keyword (`to top left`) or an angle (`90deg` = to right, `0deg` = to top).

### radial-gradient
Starts at a center point and spreads outward.
```css
background: radial-gradient(circle at center, #ff5733 0%, #ffc300 40%, #2980b9 100%);
```
Shape: `circle` or `ellipse` (default). Size keywords: `closest-side`, `farthest-corner`.

### conic-gradient
Colors rotate around a center - great for pie charts and color wheels:
```css
background: conic-gradient(red, yellow, lime, aqua, blue, magenta, red);
```

### Color stops
- Add positions: `red 20%, blue 60%`.
- Two stops at the same position make a **hard edge**: `red 50%, blue 50%`.
- Use transparency (`rgba(255,0,0,0)`) for fades.

### Repeating gradients
`repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, #d2e0fb 0 10px, #79ac78 10px 20px)` makes stripes.

### Overlay trick
Put a semi-transparent gradient above an image to darken it for readable text:
`background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(0,0,0,.5), rgba(0,0,0,.5)), url(photo.jpg);`

### Tips
- Gradients are images: use `background-size` to make patterns.
- Use `in oklch` (e.g. `linear-gradient(in oklch, blue, red)`) for smoother mixes in modern browsers.
keyPoints: Gradients are generated images used in background-image
linear (direction/angle), radial (center), conic (around a point)
Same position for two stops creates a hard edge
repeating-* variants make stripes and patterns
Layer a transparent gradient over an image for overlays
pitfalls: Using gradient with the color property (use background-clip: text)
Forgetting that 0deg points up, not right
Gradient to transparent looking gray in older browsers (use the same color with alpha 0)

interview.q: Difference between linear and radial gradients?
interview.a: Linear transitions along a straight line; radial radiates outward from a center point in a circle or ellipse.

interview.q: How do you create a hard color edge in a gradient?
interview.a: Give two adjacent color stops the same position, e.g. red 50%, blue 50%.

interview.q: How do you put a color overlay on an image?
interview.a: Use multiple backgrounds: a semi-transparent linear-gradient first, then the url() image.

topics.title: Lists and Links
topics.summary: Style bullets with list-style and links with :link, :visited, :hover, :active (LVHA order).
topics.description:
### Lists
- `list-style-type`: `disc`, `circle`, `square`, `decimal`, `lower-alpha`, `none`...
- `list-style-position`: `outside` (default) or `inside`.
- `list-style-image`: use an image as a marker.
- `list-style`: shorthand, e.g. `list-style: square inside;`.

Remove bullets for navigation menus: `ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }`. Custom markers are best done with `li::marker` or `li::before`.

### Counters
CSS counters number any element: `counter-reset`, `counter-increment`, `content: counter(name)`.

### Links and states
Anchors have several states. Style them in **LVHA** order so later ones override earlier ones:

1. `a:link` - unvisited
2. `a:visited` - already visited (only color-like properties allowed for privacy)
3. `a:hover` - mouse over
4. `a:active` - while being clicked

Also remember `:focus` and `:focus-visible` for keyboard users.

### Making a link look like a button
Anchors are inline, so set `display: inline-block;` before giving padding/width:

```css
a.btn { display: inline-block; padding: 10px 32px; border-radius: 5px; text-decoration: none; }
```

### Tips
- Keep underlines on links inside text; users rely on them.
- Provide at least 3:1 contrast between link and surrounding text if you remove underlines.
keyPoints: list-style controls type, position and image of markers
list-style: none + reset margin/padding for menus
Link states order: link, visited, hover, active (LVHA)
Use display: inline-block to size anchors
Always style :focus-visible for keyboard users
pitfalls: Writing a:hover before a:link/a:visited so hover never applies
Removing list bullets but leaving default padding-left
Removing underlines and focus outlines together (inaccessible links)

interview.q: How do you remove bullets from a list?
interview.a: list-style: none; and usually reset padding-left/margin on the ul.

interview.q: How do you make an <a> accept width, height and vertical padding?
interview.a: Make it display: inline-block (or block/flex), because inline elements ignore those.

topics.title: Images, object-fit and aspect-ratio
topics.summary: Make images responsive, crop them with object-fit and keep proportions with aspect-ratio.
topics.description:
### Responsive images
The simplest rule for fluid images:

```css
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
```
- `max-width: 100%` stops overflow.
- `height: auto` keeps the proportions.
- `display: block` removes the tiny gap below inline images.

Always set `width` and `height` attributes in HTML so the browser reserves space and avoids layout shift (CLS).

### object-fit
When an image (or video) has a fixed box, `object-fit` decides how it fills it:

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `fill` | stretches (default) |
| `contain` | fits entirely, may letterbox |
| `cover` | fills and crops, keeps ratio |
| `none` | natural size |
| `scale-down` | smaller of none or contain |

`object-position` chooses the focal point, e.g. `object-position: top;` for portraits.

### aspect-ratio
`aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;` makes a box keep a ratio without padding hacks. Use `aspect-ratio: 1;` for squares/avatars. If both width and height are set, the ratio is ignored.

### Related
- `border-radius: 50%` + `object-fit: cover` = perfect circular avatar.
- `loading="lazy"` and `srcset` / `<picture>` for performance (HTML side).
- `filter` and `clip-path` for effects (see the Visual Effects section).
keyPoints: img { max-width: 100%; height: auto } is the responsive baseline
object-fit cover/contain crops or fits media inside a fixed box
aspect-ratio replaces the padding-top hack
Set width/height attributes to prevent layout shift
object-position sets the focal point
pitfalls: Setting both width and height with different ratio and distorting the image
Using background-image for meaningful content (no alt text)
Forgetting aspect-ratio is ignored when width and height are both fixed

interview.q: How do you make an image responsive?
interview.a: max-width: 100%; height: auto; (and set width/height attributes for layout stability).
It scales the image to fill the box while keeping the aspect ratio, cropping what does not fit.

interview.q: How do you keep a 16:9 box without JavaScript?
interview.a: aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; (older approach: padding-top: 56.25% on a wrapper).
